newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank chairman sees no strong EMU opposition.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank chairman sees no strong EMU opposition.

text.p: Chairman of Sweden's central bank, Kjell-Olof Feldt, said on Tuesday that there was no strong opposition toward Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from the Swedish public.
"I see no big majority against EMU, I don't think we have this at the present time," Feldt told a conference.
"If you listen to the debate you would be surprised to hear the views among people generally."
A poll published on Monday showed that public opposition to EMU has waned in Sweden with 52 percent now in favour of Sweden joining EMU, whether at the start on January 1, 1999, or at a later date.
